5-6: Taking 1, 2 or 3 stones from a pile in turn, the one who takes the last winning or losing: the right first move.
Taking away a divisor of the number in turn, the one who cannot move losing: which first moves win.
Taking from a pile only amounts of a fixed set, such as 1, 3 or 4: a table of winning and losing positions.
Two piles of coins, any number taken from one pile in turn: equal piles and who wins.
Breaking a bar into small squares in turn: the number of breaks is fixed, so who makes the last.
Signs plus and minus put in turn between numbers: whether the result is odd or even is fixed before the game starts.
A king moved towards a corner of a board in turn: the squares to leave the other player on.
Coins in a row, one taken from either end in turn: how the first player makes sure of at least half.
Symmetry: copying the other player's moves, such as coins placed on a round table, to win.
Writing the digits of a three-digit number in turn: whether the last player can make it divisible by 3.
Numbers said in turn, each between twice and three times the last, whoever reaches a limit losing: work back from the limit in bands of numbers.
A pile from which a move takes at least one thing and at most half of it, the one left facing a single thing losing: piles one less than a power of two lose for the player to move.
Cards 1 to 9 taken in turn, three that add up to 15 winning: the game is noughts and crosses on a magic square, so it ends in a draw.
Rooks put in turn on a square board so that none attacks another: each takes a row and a column, so the game lasts as many moves as there are rows, and that decides who moves last.
Two piles where a move eats one pile and splits the other into two: the player facing two odd piles loses.
